findings.claim:
The frontmatter check can pass without finding the frontmatter. If the file does not begin with "---
", TrimPrefix leaves it unchanged. Cut then splits at the first later "
---
", so the checked region may be only a pre-fence preamble or an arbitrary slice. The test never asserts that the opening and closing fences were found (Cut's found result is discarded). A malformed or moved frontmatter therefore lets an effort field go undetected. Also, HasPrefix on the raw line no longer catches an indented key such as "  thinking: x" or a spaced key such as "effort :". The old Contains check caught the indented form, so recall drops.

If the closing fence is the last line with no trailing newline, "\n---\n" is not found. Cut then returns the whole file as the frontmatter, so body prose lines starting with "thinking:" would fail the test. That is the false positive this commit set out to remove. CRLF line endings would behave the same way.

evidence: Only engine/agentgen/foreman_test.go changed; the whole diff was read.

The new parsing relies on exact "---
" and "
---
" delimiters and discards Cut's found flag.
